inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement, ShareBasedCompensation add-back (SEC XBRL, filed 2026-08-06); Fox publishes no combined equity-award-tax line, and net-share-settlement withholding is immaterial against $2.0B of buybacks, so the add-back is used as-is
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:01Z regular close (Friday); valuation written Monday 2026-09-28 before the open
inputs.share_count_basis: 427M = Q4 FY2026 diluted weighted average, derived as 4 x FY2026 diluted (439M) - 3 x 9M FY2026 diluted (443M); the FY figure (439M) is stale after $2.0B of FY2026 repurchases concentrated in H1. Class A + Class B combined; the model values a share of either class identically (the A/B spread is a voting-rights discount the DCF does not price). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the $2.0B FY2026 buyback (4.5% of the count) and $287M dividend are the funding of that flat count, not a further per-share tailwind.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD WACC: 10y UST ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.85 -> cost of equity ~8.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~6% on $6.6B of senior notes (after-tax ~4.6%); market weights ~80/20 at $27B equity / $6.6B debt give ~7.7%, rounded up to 8.0% for a business whose 40% affiliate-fee base is in structural decline. No further ad-hoc premium: secular decline, sports-rights inflation and the Roku overhang are charged in the scenario paths and the equity bridge, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating lease liabilities ($962M at 2026-06-30) are excluded from net debt and lease cost is left inside EBITDA (operating lease expense runs through operating costs under ASC 842, so Adjusted EBITDA is already post-lease). One treatment: leases in the flows, not in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are immaterial (net income attributable to NCI ~$10-20M/yr, mostly the Fox Studio Lot and Credible); no NCI deduction and no attributable adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: US operating media company; not a bank/REIT/LIC). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. OWNER FCF: reported FCF 1,468 (OCF 1,970 - capex 502) less SBC 132 less interest income 127 = 1,209. FY2026 reported FCF is a trough year: OCF absorbed FIFA World Cup rights and production cash timing and capex stepped up to $502M (FOX One / Tubi platform build, vs $331-359M in FY2022-25); FY2025 was the mirror-image peak ($2,993M reported). The forward build therefore starts from components, not from either year's margin. ADJUSTED EBITDA: FY2026 company-reported $3.91B = 22.8% of revenue, flattered by the World Cup (Q4 advertising +78% YoY); FY2022-25 ran 20.2-22.9% ($3.2B, $3.2B, $2.9B, $3.3B), so year-1 base margin is set at 20.5% and drifts to 19.5% as sports-rights inflation (NFL renewal) outruns affiliate rate increases. INTEREST: $401M of interest expense on the notes is NOT deducted from the unlevered flows; it is charged once, through net debt in the bridge. CASH TAX: cash taxes paid ran 11-18% of pretax income in FY2024-26 (FY2026 $335M on $2,278M pretax = 14.7%) against a 24% GAAP provision, because the 2019 Disney-transaction tax-basis step-up is still being amortised; the shelter is real but finite, so the cash rate ramps 17% -> 24% over eight years rather than being perpetuated. HORIZON: 10 years, because the tax ramp and the margin drift are still moving at year 5. WORKING CAPITAL: 0% capture; ad-supported and sports-rights-prepayment businesses have no structural deferred-revenue tailwind, and the FY2025/FY2026 swings are timing. EQUITY BRIDGE: (+) $965M long-term investments at book (FY2026 10-K; the matching asset for investment income that is excluded from EBITDA); (-) Roku deal overhang, itemised in equity_bridge and explained in valuation_philosophy. Standalone (ex-Roku-bridge) values are stated in valuation_philosophy.summary so a reader who disagrees with the deal probability can strip it. NOT MODELLED: the FanDuel 18.6% option (strike ~$4.5B escalating, expires 2030) is out-of-the-money-to-marginal at current FanDuel marks and is upside not in the numbers. Interest income is stripped although net cash is negative because the $4.2B cash pile is added back through net debt: the same double-count rule applies.
inputs.adjusted_ebitda_source: Company-reported Adjusted EBITDA, Q4 FY2026 earnings release 2026-08-06 (per Analysis.json recent_developments); FY2022-25 figures from the equivalent releases

equity_bridge.note: FY2026 10-K balance sheet, LongTermInvestments (SEC XBRL). Non-operating; its income is outside Adjusted EBITDA, so the asset is added under the matching-asset rule.

equity_bridge.item: Roku deal: 50% x regulatory termination fee ($1.2B)
equity_bridge.note: Fox owes Roku ~$1.2B if the deal fails on antitrust grounds (Analysis.json risks.financial). DOJ second request issued; probability of break judged 50%.

equity_bridge.item: Roku deal: 50% x house-basis value transfer if it closes at $160/Roku share
equity_bridge.note: If the deal closes Fox pays ~$14.4B cash + ~145M FOXA shares (~$24B equity value, ~$22B EV) for a business whose owner FCF (reported FCF ~$0.4B less SBC ~$0.4B) is roughly zero before the guided $400M of synergies. On this model's basis (8% WACC, 12x cap) the Roku operations plus synergies are worth ~$8-9B and Roku brings ~$2.2B of cash; existing Fox holders end with ~74% of (standalone equity + $10.7B received - $14.4B cash paid), a loss of roughly $9B versus standalone. Charged at 50% deal-close probability = -$4.5B (~-$10.5/share). The market re-rated FOXA from ~$76 to ~$63 on the June-2026 announcement, i.e. ~-$13/share, consistent with this charge plus the fee. Strip this line for a standalone Fox value.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment anchored between equity_5yr_cagr (1.1%) and the ex-event revenue trend; revenue CAGRs are flattered by the FY2026 World Cup and FY2025 Super Bowl/election year, and the equity CAGR is depressed by $7B of buybacks and dividends, so neither is used raw
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (1.1%) is more than 30% below revenue 5yr CAGR (5.8%): the gap is capital return ($1.0-2.0B/yr of buybacks plus dividends), not value destruction. EPS 3yr CAGR (18.7%) is off the FY2023 Dominion-settlement trough and is not a trend.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2021->FY2026 (5yr) and FY2023->FY2026 (3yr) from Metrics.csv. Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2021 2,004; FY2022 1,469; FY2023 1,238; FY2024 1,216; FY2025 2,682; FY2026 1,209. The owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (-9.6%) sits below the reported-FCF CAGR (-7.4%) because interest income on the cash pile grew from $4M to $127M over the period while SBC held flat; the end points are also a peak-to-trough pairing (FY2021 strong OCF; FY2026 World Cup cash absorption and elevated capex), so the negative CAGR describes cash timing, not a shrinking business: Adjusted EBITDA rose from ~$2.9B to $3.9B over the same window.

base.narrative: FY2027 revenue -2%: the Q4 FY2026 World Cup advertising comp is only partly offset by the World Cup knockout rounds landing in Q1 FY2027, midterm-election political advertising at the owned stations and the Super Bowl rotation. FY2028 flat, then ~1.5-2% as Tubi (+25% FY2026) and FOX One offset mid-single-digit affiliate subscriber losses. Margin 20.5% (FY2022-25 average, below the World Cup-flattered 22.8%) drifting to 19.5% as the next NFL renewal escalates rights cost. Capex normalises from the FY2026 $502M platform build toward 2.3% of revenue. Cash tax ramps 17% -> 24% as the Disney-separation step-up amortises out.

bull.narrative: Live news and sports prove as bundle-resistant as management claims: affiliate rate increases fully offset subscriber losses, FOX One converts cord-nevers at $20/month without cannibalising retrans, Tubi keeps compounding at 20%+ and reaches mid-teens EBITDA margins, and the advertising market shifts CTV dollars to Fox's owned FAST inventory. Margin expands to 22.5% (the FY2022 level) as digital revenue outgrows rights cost. Terminal cap 14x, still below the 20x default for a mature compounder because the linear base is in decline.

bear.narrative: Cord-cutting accelerates to high-single-digit subscriber losses and vMVPDs push back on Fox News/FS1 carriage rates; an advertising downturn hits the 45% ad line just as the World Cup comp rolls off; the NFL renewal lifts rights cost faster than revenue and Fox pays to keep the package. Tubi's growth is absorbed by a Roku Channel/Pluto price war. Revenue shrinks ~2%/yr, margin compresses to 15.5%, terminal growth 0% and a 10x cap for a melting-ice-cube linear asset. Cash taxes still ramp to 24%.

scenario_narratives.base: Fox remains a slowly shrinking linear business (affiliate fees ~40% of revenue in structural decline) whose live-sports and Fox News scarcity holds pricing, while Tubi and FOX One grow fast enough to keep total revenue roughly flat to +1.5% and Adjusted EBITDA near $3.4-3.7B. Capital return continues at $1-2B/yr. The Roku deal is a coin-flip on DOJ clearance and is carried as an expected-value charge in the bridge rather than as a fourth scenario.
scenario_narratives.bull: Live news and sports are the last must-have linear content; affiliate rate cards keep rising, FOX One and Tubi become material profit centres, ad dollars follow engagement to owned CTV inventory, and the combined business re-rates toward a 14x cash-flow multiple. If the Roku deal closes and the platform thesis works, distribution ownership and first-party data add optionality beyond this scenario's numbers.
scenario_narratives.bear: The pay-TV bundle unwinds faster than digital can replace it, the NFL renewal is dilutive, an ad recession compounds the World Cup comp, and Tubi's economics are competed away by Roku Channel and Pluto. Fox becomes a cash-return story with declining cash: revenue -2%/yr, margin to 15.5%, terminal growth zero, 10x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25% because the affiliate-fee base is in unambiguous structural decline, profitability is concentrated in two assets (Fox News ratings and the NFL package) with an escalating renewal ahead, and the pending Roku transaction adds regulatory and balance-sheet uncertainty on top. Bull cut to 25% because it requires several independent things to go right at once (FOX One scaling without cannibalisation, Tubi margin expansion, ad-market strength, and a benign NFL renewal). Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Fox is valued as a standalone, slowly shrinking but highly cash-generative live-news-and-sports business on a fully SBC-expensed, unlevered owner-FCF basis, discounted at 8% with a 12x terminal cap (bull 14x, bear 10x) instead of Gordon growth, because a buyer of a linear-media cash stream does not pay a compounder's multiple. The FY2026 trough (World Cup cash absorption, capex step-up) and FY2025 peak reported FCFs are both ignored in favour of a component build off a 20.5% Adjusted EBITDA margin. The pending ~$22B Roku acquisition is the dominant swing factor: on a house basis Roku's owner FCF is roughly zero before synergies, so closing at $160/share is value-dilutive to Fox holders by roughly $9B, and failing costs a ~$1.2B fee. Both are carried at 50% probability in the equity bridge (-$5.1B, ~-$12/share in total). Standalone ex-Roku values are the engine values plus ~$12/share; a reader who believes the deal is blocked with no fee, or that Roku's platform is worth its price, should adjust the bridge, not the operating drivers.
key_risks_to_valuation: DOJ blocks, delays or restructures the Roku deal: a clean block (no fee) is +$1.4/share vs the bridge; a close at full terms is roughly -$10/share vs the bridge on this model's basis
NFL and other sports-rights renewals lift programming cost faster than affiliate and ad revenue, pushing margin below the 19.5% base terminal level
Pay-TV subscriber losses accelerate beyond mid-single digits or vMVPDs drop Fox News/FS1, eroding the ~40% affiliate-fee base faster than Tubi/FOX One replace it
Advertising cyclicality: ~45% of revenue is ad-driven and FY2026 carried a non-recurring World Cup boost; a recession would push FY2027-28 below the base path
Cash tax shelter from the Disney-separation step-up expires sooner than the eight-year ramp assumes, or the statutory rate rises
Fox News litigation (Dominion-type defamation exposure) and the dual-class control structure, which lets the controlling family pursue transformative M&A over minority objection
Upside not modelled: FanDuel option, a Roku deal renegotiated to better terms, and any re-rating if FOX One scales to a material subscription business
